CurrentLocation: In situ, City of David, Jerusalem
Description: A monumental Iron Age building in the City of David, excavated by Eilat Mazar from 2005: massive stone walls, a large hall, and fine masonry on the ridge above the Kidron Valley. Mazar identified it as the palace of King David; other archaeologists date parts of it later and dispute the identification, while all agree it was a major public building of the early monarchy.
BiblicalSignificance: 2 Samuel says David captured Jerusalem, built up the city around, and raised a palace of cedar. Whether these exact walls are that palace or a later king's, they prove Jerusalem in the tenth century was no village — it was a capital with monumental architecture, ruled by a king strong enough to build in stone.
